title: Spillover Effects of Opioid Abuse on Skilled Human Capital and Innovation Activity
authors: Kimberly Rodgers Cornaggia; John E. Hund; Kevin J Pisciotta; Ziming Ye
eligible_reason: Single common shock date with continuous exposure: post2010 = 1 for year >= 2010 for every county (OxyContin reformulation), interacted with continuous county opioid-abuse exposure (didvar = oxyqtypoprate5_100[_win5/_win25], CMS prescribing rate; alternatives totoxy_c_00_pc, chgoxy97_00_c_pc). Statacode_CHPY.do: reghdfe/ppmlhdfe y c.`didvar'##1.post2010 [+ baseline covariates x post2010], a(fips state_year) cluster(state_year); event studies interact the continuous exposure with year indicators. One adoption date and a continuous dose, so no staggered binary design. Several outcomes use Poisson (ppmlhdfe).
design_notes: County-year panel 1999-2019 (Countylevelfilemasked.dta, 65,898 rows) with county FE and state x year FE; state-year panel (Statelevelfile.dta) with state FE and region x year FE for ACS/LEHD outcomes (initial_oxy x post2010). Tables cover IRS net outflows, inventor and research-lab out-migration (PPML with exposure), patent counts/value, school quality, local spending, crime, and first-stage/exogenous-exposure (pre-sample oxycodone) versions. Cross-sectional splits interact post2010 x exposure x highmovers.
data_files_note: Readme.pdf: the public Countylevelfilemasked.dta 'does not include the true nature of the variable oxyqtypoprate5_100' (restricted CMS data), and opioid mortality controls, the pre-sample oxycodone exposure measures, and CoreLogic inventor home sales are also masked; the log (replication.smcl) was produced on the unmasked file. CDC mortality microdata for Figure 1 not shipped. Inspected: oxyqtypoprate5_100_win5 has mean 0.004, SD 0.92, consistent with a masked/replaced variable.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Common 2010 shock with continuous exposure; not staggered. Treatment variable masked in the shipped data in any case.
